news.title: Docker drops the box-carrying whale for “Run on Trust”
news.summary: Docker unveiled a new identity on 19 November: a simplified whale with a containment symbol, a new signature blue (#6172FF) and a new line, “Run on Trust”. The pitch moves from shipping containers to running software and AI agents safely.
news.take: When your product’s job changes, the logo has to stop describing the old job. The whale stays, the boxes go, and that’s exactly the right amount of change.

news.title: Maker’s Mark gets a new identity, dipped in red wax
news.summary: Turner Duckworth has redesigned the identity of the Kentucky bourbon brand, built around the hand-dipped red wax seal that has been on its bottles for decades.
news.take: Own one thing so completely that it becomes the brand. Maker’s Mark wax is bourbon’s Tiffany blue, and the redesign is smart enough to lean in.

news.title: GTA VI lands, and so does an influencer kit with bite
news.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI launched on 19 November. Birmingham agency Fluid marked it with “Xbox Has More Bite”, an influencer kit sent to 80 creators across eight countries.
news.take: For the biggest launch of the year, the smart play wasn’t a billboard. It was 80 parcels designed to be unboxed on camera.

news.title: FutureBrand says the “finished brand” is over
news.summary: Relaunching itself, FutureBrand argues that static identity systems can’t keep up now that brands appear everywhere and more of their output is made by AI. Its answer is designing “brand behaviour”: how a brand looks, moves, talks and sounds, and how an AI trained on it makes decisions. The report, From Artefact to Infinite, came out on 18 November.
news.take: Half of this is agency positioning, half is true. If an AI is going to make your ads, your guidelines need rules for judgement, not just logo clear-space.

news.title: Koto gives Giffgaff a signpost-led rebrand
news.summary: UK mobile network Giffgaff has a new identity from London studio Koto, built around the idea of signposts pointing customers to their next chapter.
news.take: Telecom branding is usually tariffs in a trench coat. A wayfinding idea at least gives the brand something to say besides price.

news.title: Adobe MAX 2026: your AI assistant can now use Photoshop
news.summary: At MAX in Miami Beach (10–12 November), Adobe spread its Creative Agent across Creative Cloud, put Firefly Design and Firefly Graph into public beta, and previewed local MCP connections that let outside agents such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini edit native Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and After Effects files.
news.take: The interesting bit isn’t another generator. It’s Adobe admitting your favourite AI might not be Adobe’s, and building the door anyway.

news.title: Google starts its November 2026 core update
news.summary: Google began rolling out its third broad core update of 2026 on 10 November, for all sites and languages. It says the rollout may take up to two weeks, and advises waiting until it finishes before reading Search Console data.
news.take: Rankings will wobble right before Black Friday. Don’t rewrite your site mid-rollout; measure a full week after it ends.

news.title: Christmas ad season opens with stop-motion and cartoons
news.summary: Early standouts in the 2026 festive ad season include a handcrafted stop-motion film from Levi’s and Prada’s cartoon wonderland directed by former Disney animator John Pomeroy.
news.take: Craft is the new flex. In a feed full of AI-smooth video, visibly handmade work gets noticed.

news.title: Koto: every electric car brand looks the same
news.summary: Branding studio Koto published a piece arguing that electric car brands have converged on one look: minimal wordmarks, soft gradients and the same calm, techy tone.
news.take: Blanding has reached the car park. If your category all looks alike, the cheapest advantage left is a personality.

news.title: John Lewis’s Christmas ad: hated online, loved by the testers
news.summary: Gloria and Pickles, the 2026 John Lewis Christmas ad starring Dame Kristin Scott Thomas, drew a fierce online backlash, with YouTube comments switched off. Yet System1 scored it 5.6 stars, the retailer’s best festive result since Excitable Edgar in 2019.
news.take: Twitter is not your customer. The loudest reaction and the most effective ad are often different things, and this year proves it.

news.title: How&How becomes HOW+HOW, with a website built for AI search
news.summary: The London and LA studio renamed itself HOW+HOW after six years, with a volume-dial logo, a new strategy and a site designed to be read by AI search as well as people.
news.take: When a branding studio designs its own site for AI readers, take the hint. Being quotable by machines is now part of the brief.

news.title: Affinity finally comes to iPad, free
news.summary: Canva’s Affinity, the free pro app for vector, photo and layout work, has arrived on iPad, giving illustrators a free all-in-one option on the tablet.
news.take: The cheapest serious design kit on the market just got portable. Freelancers paying for three subscriptions should do some maths this weekend.

news.title: Figma brings code layers and Config to India
news.summary: At its biggest international Config yet, in India on 15 October, Figma moved code layers into open beta, so teams can build code-backed prototypes on the canvas, and announced an education programme and an MCP partnership with Sarvam.
news.take: Design files are turning into working software. Learn enough code to read what the canvas now produces.

news.title: Google’s September spam update finishes after 14 days
news.summary: Google’s September 2026 spam update completed around 8 October after nearly two weeks, the longest spam rollout of the year.
news.take: Spam updates hit scaled, thin and copied content. If your blog is mostly reworded AI summaries, this is your warning shot.

news.title: Canva lowers its growth forecast as AI costs bite
news.summary: Canva cut its expected annual revenue growth from 30% to 20% in August 2026, a slowdown reported alongside the rising cost of the AI features it offers.
news.take: Even the design-for-everyone giant is finding AI expensive to give away. Expect more credit limits and paid tiers across every tool you use.

news.title: Blinkit’s lead keeps widening
news.summary: Blinkit handled about 331 million orders in the April–June 2026 quarter and ended it with 2,443 stores, nearly three times Instamart’s order volume.
news.take: Scale is turning into range, and range into habit. Challengers now need a reason to be opened that isn’t speed.

news.title: Flipkart Minutes passes 1,000 fulfilment centres
news.summary: Flipkart’s quick-commerce arm crossed 1,000 micro-fulfilment centres across 130+ cities, with a target of about 1,500 by the end of 2026.
news.take: Expect electronics and non-grocery categories to be where Flipkart picks its fights.

news.title: Figma pushes into marketing assets
news.summary: Alongside Make (prompt to prototype) and Sites, Figma launched Buzz for producing on-brand marketing assets at scale from designer-controlled templates.
news.take: If your brand system lives in Figma, Buzz may replace a lot of Canva work. If it lives in Canva, stay put.

news.title: Zepto’s IPO paperwork moves ahead
news.summary: Zepto reportedly received SEBI’s go-ahead and filed an updated draft prospectus, which also published rare side-by-side order data for Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart.
news.take: Prospectuses are the best free market research in India. Read the peer tables, not the headlines.

news.title: Blinkit’s founder now runs Eternal
news.summary: Deepinder Goyal stepped down as Eternal group CEO from 1 February 2026; Blinkit founder Albinder Dhindsa took over, with Goyal staying on as vice chairman.
news.take: The parent brand was renamed for this moment: the biggest business now leads a group named after none of its apps.

news.title: Canva relaunches Affinity as a free pro app
news.summary: Canva relaunched Affinity as a single free desktop app for vector, photo and layout work; its AI features need a paid Canva plan.
news.take: The best free alternative to Creative Cloud for logos, print and packaging. Budget for AI credits separately.
